title: A stand-in test matches its target's interactions
statement: A test standing in for another must reproduce its interactions, navigation rules and per-sitting format mix, since a different interface changes how students respond and what scores mean.
example: One stand-in reading test requires at least 12 technology-enhanced items in every 40-item session.
detail: A stand-in for an outside reading test follows that test's documented interaction conventions, forward-only navigation, an answer before each advance and all six item interactions, so that its scores stay comparable and the official test measures reading rather than interface novelty (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/MAP_PROXY_VALIDITY_CASE.md`). It argues from response-process validity in the testing standards: students who interact with items differently on another platform respond differently, and their scores are not comparable. Its design review makes a floor of 12 technology-enhanced items per 40-item session a hard constraint and counts an all-multiple-choice session as a violation (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/skill/SKILL.md`).
against: Parity is partial: of the six formats, three are confirmed for the reference test's reading levels, two are documented only for its other subjects and one only in secondary materials (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/map-proxy-assessment/validity/MAP_PROXY_VALIDITY_CASE.md`, line 92).

evidence.quote: If students interact with items differently on our platform than on MAP — different cognitive load from an unfamiliar UI, different navigation affordances, different format rendering — response patterns will differ and scores will not be comparable.
The interface follows MAP's publicly documented interaction conventions, so that students experience familiar testing conventions and the official test measures reading rather than interface novelty:
**Forward-only navigation**: once an item is answered, it is locked; no back button
**TE floor ≥12 per 40-item session** — every format except plain MCQ counts as TE (MSQ, EBSR, hot-text, sequence, match/gap-match)

citations.ref: AERA, APA & NCME 2014, Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing
